T: Last train of the night. Snacks for the platform.
D: Two foster brothers, both transit cops, plan to rob the train that collects subway fares.
P: Pour drinks when the money train pulls into the station.
S: grabbed on the subway station shift
Small pastry half-moons filled with spiced beef and olives, crimped and baked at 200C for 20 minutes.
eat them quick, before the Torch turns up

Mixed nuts tossed in honey, sugar, cinnamon and a pinch of salt, roasted at 170C for 15 minutes, stirred as they cool so they don't clump. Toss 300g mixed nuts with 2 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp caster sugar, 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon and a pinch of salt. Spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 15 minutes, stirring halfway. Keep stirring as they cool so they don't clump.
round, gold and stamped like a subway token
Shortbread rounds pressed with a token-sized cutter and a cut-out middle, baked at 160C for 15 minutes, brushed with edible gold.
M: Beef mince and onion chopped together on a hot griddle with salt and adobo seasoning, American cheese melted through, into a hero roll with lettuce, tomato, mayo and ketchup.
Grace, the cop they both fall for, and her Puerto Rican cooking
Brown chicken thighs, then sofrito (onion, capsicum, garlic, coriander), annatto, rice, olives, capers and stock. Chicken back on top, covered, 25 minutes.
W: a Puerto Rican bakery by the station
Flaky puff pastry squares filled with guava paste and cream cheese, glazed with syrup. Cut 2 sheets puff pastry into 8 squares each.
K: a whole train full of fare money, too tempting for Charlie

Cold lager with lime, tomato juice, hot sauce and Worcestershire in a chilli-salted glass, served brown-paper-bag style. Mix 1 tbsp flaky salt with 1 tsp chilli powder. Rub a lime wedge around 4 glass rims and dip in the salt. Add ice, 30ml lime juice, 60ml tomato juice, 4 dashes hot sauce and 2 dashes Worcestershire to each glass. Top each with a 375ml cold lager, stir gently and slip the glasses into small paper bags.

steps.text: Toss the nuts with the honey, sugar, cinnamon and salt until coated.
Spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C, stirring halfway.
Keep stirring as they cool so they do not clump.
Beat the butter and icing sugar until pale, then mix in the flour to a soft dough.
Chill the dough for 15 minutes so it rolls cleanly.
Roll 5mm thick, cut rounds the size of a subway token and cut a small hole from the middle of each.
Bake at 160C until just set and pale gold.
Cool on the tray, then brush with gold dust mixed with a drop of water.

dishes.make_ahead: Up to 1 day, reheat with a splash of stock

steps.text: Brown the chicken in a wide lidded pan until golden, then set aside.
Fry the onion, capsicum, garlic and coriander in the same pan until soft.
Stir in the annatto, rice, olives, capers and stock and bring to a simmer.
Sit the chicken on top, cover and cook on low until the rice is tender.
Rest, covered, before serving.

dishes.make_ahead: Up to 1 day, crisp in the oven before serving

steps.text: Thaw the pastry, then cut each sheet into 8 squares.
Put a slice of guava paste and a little cream cheese on half the squares, cover with the rest and seal the edges with a fork.
Bake at 200C until puffed and golden.
Simmer the sugar with the water for a few minutes to make a syrup, then brush it over the warm pastries.

ingredients.item: limes, juiced, with some cut into wedges

steps.text: Mix the salt and chilli powder on a plate.
Rub a lime wedge around each of 4 glass rims and dip in the chilli salt.
Add ice a good squeeze of lime juice, the tomato juice, hot sauce and Worcestershire, dividing evenly.
Top each with a cold lager, stir gently and slip the glasses into small paper bags.
Split each bun and spread the inside with butter.
Press in a hot dry pan or sandwich press until golden and warm through.
Bury in icing sugar and serve straight away.

ingredients.item: lengths Cuban or soft white bread, about 20cm

steps.text: Split the bread and spread the cut sides with mustard.
Layer the pork, ham, cheese and pickles, then close.
Butter the outside and press in a hot pan or sandwich press until the cheese melts and the crust is crisp.

dishes.make_ahead: Roast a day ahead and reheat

ingredients.item: sour orange juice, or half orange and half lime juice
cooked red beans, tinned and drained

steps.text: Score the pork skin. Pound the garlic, oregano and salt to a paste with the juice and oil.
Rub the paste deep into the pork and marinate in the fridge overnight, or at least 4 hours.
Roast at 150C, covered with foil, until the meat falls apart.
Remove the foil, raise to 220C and roast until the skin crackles.
Cook the rice while the pork rests, and warm the red beans.
Rest the pork before pulling and serving with the rice and beans.

ingredients.item: thin cut beef top round steak

steps.text: Season the steak with salt and half the garlic.
Sear the steak in batches in hot oil and set aside.
Soften the onions in the pan, add the remaining garlic, oregano and vinegar and return the steak.
Cover and simmer gently until tender.
Cook the rice. Slice the plantains thickly, fry, smash flat and fry again for tostones.
Stir the sugar into the milk until dissolved.
Whisk in the orange juice just before serving.
Pour over crushed ice in tall glasses.

s.how: Toss 300g mixed nuts with 2 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp caster sugar, 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon and a pinch of salt. Spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 15 minutes, stirring halfway. Keep stirring as they cool so they don't clump.

s.note: round, gold and stamped like a subway token
s.how: Beat 200g soft butter with 100g icing sugar and mix in 300g plain flour to a dough. Roll 5mm thick, cut rounds the size of a subway token and cut a small hole from the middle of each. Bake at 160C for 15 minutes and cool. Brush with edible gold dust mixed with a drop of water.

m.note: Grace, the cop they both fall for, and her Puerto Rican cooking
m.how: Brown 800g chicken thighs and set aside. Fry 1 onion, 1 capsicum, 3 garlic cloves and a handful of coriander until soft, add 1 tsp ground annatto, 300g long grain rice, 60g green olives, 1 tbsp capers and 650ml chicken stock. Sit the chicken on top, cover and cook on low for 25 minutes until the rice is tender.

w.note: a Puerto Rican bakery by the station
w.how: Cut 2 sheets puff pastry into 8 squares each. Put a slice of guava paste and a little cream cheese on half, cover with the rest and seal. Bake at 200C for 20 minutes and brush with sugar syrup.

d.note: Cold lager with lime, tomato juice, hot sauce and Worcestershire in a chilli-salted glass, served brown-paper-bag style.
d.how: Mix 1 tbsp flaky salt with 1 tsp chilli powder. Rub a lime wedge around 4 glass rims and dip in the salt. Add ice, 30ml lime juice, 60ml tomato juice, 4 dashes hot sauce and 2 dashes Worcestershire to each glass. Top each with a 375ml cold lager, stir gently and slip the glasses into small paper bags.
